# AUMLOK lane — provenance and the measured compatibility mapping

**Source pin:** `aukora-deep` `c417f7c5752bf14b8e927986cd995f2e086f4189` (2026-09-15 19:49:06 −07:00,
*"Merge pull request #311 from aumara-xyz/ops/rv3-cutover-kit"*). Nothing in this lane writes to Deep.

**What "measured at the pin" means (corrected 2026-09-26).** The vectors were generated by Deep's own
modules, imported from a Deep checkout at `7be3a614` with no tracked modifications. That commit is a
sibling of the pin `c417f7c5`, not a descendant. The script checks only that the pin object exists in the
repository. For every Deep module named in this document, the git blob at `7be3a614` is identical to the
one at the pin (checked with `git rev-parse <commit>:<path>`, not by the script). `@noble/post-quantum`
came from the checkout's untracked `node_modules`.

**Instrument:** `scripts/aumlok/regenerate-deep-vectors.mjs` runs Deep's own modules at the pin and
writes `tests/fixtures/aumlok/deep-compatibility-vectors.json` (sha256
`3796b8f42bae3a60a1a26f526ccc11883c23c9f9913cc2ca16814f753f37a50a`, public material only — no seed,
private key or secret). The court fails if any digest this lane computes stops matching Deep's.

```bash
node scripts/aumlok/regenerate-deep-vectors.mjs --deep <deep-checkout> --check   # reviewer, needs a Deep checkout
node tests/aukora-aumlok.test.mjs                                                # the lane's own court, needs nothing else
```

The regeneration script refuses modified tracked files in the Deep checkout and refuses a checkout
whose repository lacks the pin object (it does not check that the checkout is AT the pin). Untracked entries are recorded in the fixture
(`source.untrackedEntriesObserved`) rather than silently assumed away, because "the checkout was
clean" would be a stronger claim than the measurement supports.

## 1. What was imported, and what was left

The rule is AGENTS.md's: *"Import only measured dependencies plus explicitly justified files"* and
*"Do not copy the old repository's documentation forest."* So this lane ports the identity modules
it actually needs and refuses the rest of the closure.

| Deep module at the pin | This lane | Relationship |
|---|---|---|
| `aukora/kernel-seed/canonical-json.mjs` | `lib/canonical.mjs` | Port. Byte-identical to Deep on the eight fixture vectors and the subject preimage, and the control-head and delegation digests computed with it match Deep's; there is no generative comparison. **Refuses** the values Deep maps to `null` (see §3.1). |
| `aukora/identity/validation.mjs` | `lib/validation.mjs` | Port, behaviour unchanged. These readers are what make a record *closed*. |
| `aukora/identity/genesis.mjs` | `lib/genesis.mjs` | Port, behaviour unchanged. Same domains, same subject preimage. |
| `aukora/identity/control.mjs` | `lib/control.mjs` | Port of the field inventories, transition rules, refusal names and digest preimages. The cryptographic boundary is made explicit instead of assumed (see §3.2). |
| `aukora/identity/delegation.mjs` | `lib/delegation.mjs` | Port, behaviour unchanged. Same attenuation rules and refusal names. |
| `aukora/identity/local-control-store.mjs` | `lib/store.mjs` | **Reader only:** no create, write, rotation or key generation. It reads Deep-format records (same shape and custody checks as Deep) and v3 records, and adds two refusal codes Deep does not have (`aumlok-local:no-private-half-in-v2`, `aumlok-local:machine-key-malformed`). One named entry point, `readLocalAumlokFullRecord`, returns the private half of a Deep-format record to the correspondence check in `identity-correspondence.mjs`, and refuses a v3 record by name. |
| `aukora/identity/broker-state.mjs` → `admitIdentityControl` | `lib/projection.mjs` → `admitPublicControl` | Same five refusal names under the `aumlok:` prefix, plus D1's DID-from-key rule. |
| `aukora/supervisor/developer-aumlok.mjs` → `projectDeveloperAumlok` | `lib/projection.mjs` → `projectPublicControl` | The public projection, widened from five fields to seven (see §3.4). |

**Deliberately not imported.** `../broker/subject-authority.mjs`, `../broker/effect-definition.mjs`,
`../host-dsh/src/grant-v5.mjs`, `identity/recovery-*.mjs`, `identity/disposable-recovery.mjs`, and Deep's
supervisor/protocol/guest modules; they belong to the broker, authority and recovery lanes, which are not
mine. `@noble/curves` and `@noble/post-quantum` are not imported as packages. Since the ML-DSA-65 repair,
`lib/vendor/noble-ml-dsa/` vendors `@noble/post-quantum@0.6.1` plus two `@noble/curves` modules, pinned.
They are used for key generation and for the sign/verify correspondence proofs (`pq-generator.mjs`,
`identity-correspondence.mjs`). They are not supplied as the promotion verifier (§3.2).

**The import closure of the ported code.** The court reads the top-level `lib/*.mjs` files and requires
every static `from '…'` specifier to be `node:*` or `./…`. It does not read `lib/vendor/**` or dynamic
`import()`. In the pinned release `@deepseek-ai/cordis` resolves only inside a workspace package, so
`lib/service.mjs` imports no package, only sibling modules, and registers through
`ctx.provide(name, value, check)` — the mechanism Cordis's own `Service` base class calls. The arm that enforces this is
*"every module in lib/ imports only node: builtins or its own siblings"*.

## 2. The compatibility mapping between the two layers

Deep's **hybrid root-control** implementation and Genesis's **Ed25519 action signer** are different
layers, and this lane changes neither. Here is the one place they are joined, measured.

1. Deep's local store writes **one** Ed25519 key pair into **two** places: the public half into
   `activeControl.publicKeys.ed25519` (the hybrid root control head), and the private half into
   `ed25519PrivateKeyPem` (the key the action signer uses).
   `local-control-store.mjs` `parseRecord` asserts the two correspond:
   `rawEd25519PublicKey(createPublicKey(ed25519PrivateKey)) === activeControl.publicKeys.ed25519`.
2. At check-at-use, `broker-state.mjs` `admitIdentityControl` requires the action-signing key's raw
   hex to equal `state.publicKeys.ed25519`, refusing otherwise with
   `broker:identity-control-signer-mismatch`.

**Consequence for this adapter.** That single equality is the whole join. The adapter therefore
exposes it as `approvalKeyDid = did:key(activeControl.publicKeys.ed25519)` (Genesis plan D1), and its
admission refusal `aumlok:control-signer-mismatch` is the same rule Deep states as `SIGNER_MISMATCH`,
computed from the key rather than matched as a string. Nothing else crosses between the layers:
`verifyAndApplyRootControlPromotion` never signs, `admitPublicControl` never returns authority, and
the action signer is the D2 channel described in §5, not part of this join.

**What a rotation does, measured.** The court takes one identity through an epoch 0 → 1 root-key
rotation using a promotion Deep itself produced and signed at the pin, and asserts:

| Fact | Behaviour across the rotation |
|---|---|
| `subject` | **unchanged**. It is a domain-separated `sha256` over the canonical genesis record, which no transition rewrites, and any change to that record yields a different subject; derived from genesis and asserted equal to the head's claim |
| `epoch` | 0 → 1 |
| `activeControlDigest` | changes (it covers the whole head) |
| `approvalKeyDid` | changes — it is the `did:key` of the newly registered Ed25519 key |
| pre-rotation delegation chain, checked against the **old** digest | verifies, with Deep's own child digest `3a8ae84e…c984ce` |
| the same chain checked against the **new** digest | refused `delegation:control-mismatch` |
| the same chain admitted against the **new** digest | refused `aumlok:control-digest-mismatch` |

That is "key rotation must not silently change the Kira subject or widen scope" as a measurement
rather than a convention.

### 2.1 Fixture compatibility is NOT production rotation verification

These are two different claims and this lane earns only the first. Stated plainly because the arm
that shows the rotation succeeding is the one most likely to be misread:

- **Fixture compatibility — EARNED.** The promotion in the fixture is *real data Deep produced and
  signed* at the pin, the epoch-1 head the transition rules compute is byte-identical to Deep's, and
  the Ed25519 half of that verification is real `node:crypto` (a flipped signature byte is caught by
  a separate arm). What this proves is that the field inventories, the digest preimages, the
  predecessor binding and the transition rules agree with Deep's.
- **Production rotation verification — NOT CLAIMED, AND NOT POSSIBLE IN THIS CLOSURE.** The accepting
  arm passes **injected test doubles** for the ML-DSA-65 verifier and the Ed25519 point validator.
  With only the primitives this closure ships, *the same promotion refuses by name* — that is what the
  three fail-closed arms measure, and that refusal is the production behaviour, not the exception.

The court prints both statements into its own output, immediately after the accepting arm, so a reader
of the evidence cannot see the green arm without seeing what it does not mean.

**Fail-closed, by name, on the default path:**

| Missing primitive | Refusal | Arm |
|---|---|---|
| anything (no `capabilities` at all) | `aumlok:ed25519-point-validator-unavailable` | *"with NO capabilities the promotion refuses by name (fail closed)"* |
| `node:crypto` only — real Ed25519, no curve library | `aumlok:ed25519-point-validator-unavailable` | *"with node:crypto alone the promotion still refuses by name (no point validator)"* |
| a point validator but no post-quantum verifier | `aumlok:ml-dsa-65-verifier-unavailable` | *"with a point validator but NO ML-DSA-65 verifier it refuses by name"* |

(The middle row's "no curve library" is about the **capability object**, not the tree: since the
ML-DSA-65 repair this closure *does* carry two `@noble/curves` modules — `utils.js` and
`abstract/fft.js` — vendored for ML-DSA's FFT. `lib/ed25519-point.mjs` holds a hand-written Ed25519 point
validator, exported from `index.mjs`, that nothing wires in and no court tests **[CODE ONLY]**.
`nodeCryptoVerifierCapabilities()` does not supply it, so the refusal is unchanged.)

Both refusals sit **after** the structural transition rules, so a caller can always tell a rule
violation (`control:predecessor-digest-mismatch`) from an unavailable primitive. Neither is ever
silently skipped, and neither can be avoided by supplying a partial capability set.

**Test doubles never reach a live profile, and the mount is measured without them.**
`tests/aukora-aumlok-mount.test.mjs` boots a disposable DSH profile from a real release with the
plugin loaded by the **real Cordis loader** from an absolute composition path, and a second plugin
that declares `inject = ['aumlokControl']` consuming it. Three facts from that run:

- The mount row carries `directory` and **nothing else** — an arm asserts on the patch text that no
  `capabilities` key exists anywhere in it.
- With no doubles configured, a real promotion through the *mounted service* comes back
  `{ok: false, reason: 'aumlok:ed25519-point-validator-unavailable'}` — the same refusal the library
  court measures, so the host does not soften it.
- The **negative control**: the same consumer mounted with no aumlok row at all does not activate,
  because Cordis withholds an unsatisfied injected dependency. The bound boot's report is therefore
  evidence of reachability and not merely of a consumer running.

The doubles themselves still exist only inside `tests/aukora-aumlok.test.mjs`'s own process and the
disposable copies `--mutate` writes under `TMPDIR`.

**PACKAGED, AND NOW MOUNTED UNBOUND (corrected 2026-09-26).** `scripts/materialize-aukora-release.py`
lists the plugin in `LANE_PLUGINS`, so a release carries it, and the materializer's default composition
patch and `aukora-lanes.patch.yml` both name a row for the service. The row carries no config, so
`refresh()` refuses `aumlok:adapter-unbound`, promotions refuse by name, and no test double can reach a
profile through it. `scripts/aumlok/diagnose.mjs` scans only `tests/fixtures` and `profiles/`, so it does
not see this row.

## 3. Measured differences from Deep

Each difference is deliberate, named, and printed as a ceiling.

### 3.1 Canonical JSON: refuse instead of silently rewriting

Deep maps `undefined`, functions, symbols and bigints to `null` at the top level and inside arrays,
and drops object properties holding them. So a field that has lost its value is re-signed as `null`
rather than flagged. This lane **refuses** those values, and refuses floats and `-0` too
(`JSON.stringify(-0)` is `"0"`, which changes the signed bytes; Deep's own `readNonNegativeInteger`
already refuses `-0`).

This is narrower than Deep on inputs this lane never produces: every record reaching the encoder is
already a closed, validated record of strings, safe integers, booleans, nulls and arrays. For every
such value the bytes are identical to Deep's — measured on eight vectors, including the astral-key
case where UTF-16 code-unit ordering and UTF-8 byte ordering disagree
(`{"😀":2,"ﬀ":1}`, which pins the ordering choice).

### 3.2 Two checks are named, not skipped

`node:crypto` (OpenSSL) is the Ed25519 primitive. This closure vendors `@noble/post-quantum`
(ML-DSA-65), used for key generation and correspondence proofs, and two `@noble/curves` helper modules. It
supplies neither as a verifier capability. AGENTS.md forbids writing a curve implementation, yet
`lib/ed25519-point.mjs` is a hand-written point validator (unwired and uncourted). Two checks Deep performs
are therefore not performed here:

* **`@noble/curves` rejects small-order and torsion Ed25519 public keys.** Parsing here checks length
  and hex only. That is a *superset* of Deep's accepted inputs and it is **fail-open**, so it is never
  allowed to reach a verdict: `verifyAndApplyRootControlPromotion` refuses
  `aumlok:ed25519-point-validator-unavailable` unless a point validator is supplied.
* **`@noble/post-quantum` verifies the ML-DSA-65 half of the hybrid suite.** This closure now
  **carries** that implementation — `plugins/aukora-aumlok/lib/vendor/noble-ml-dsa/`, pinned to
  `@noble/post-quantum@0.6.1`, used by `lib/pq-generator.mjs` to generate and prove the binding
  keypair — but it does not *supply* it as a verifier: `nodeCryptoVerifierCapabilities()` still
  returns Ed25519 verification only, so a promotion refuses `aumlok:ml-dsa-65-verifier-unavailable`
  rather than verifying one half of a two-half signature and calling it verified. Wiring the vendored
  verifier into the default capability set is a separate change with its own evidence and is **not**
  made here. What the vendored implementation IS used for today is generation and correspondence
  proofs: `bind` and `make-disposable-identity.mjs` produce a real pair and prove it corresponds before
  registering it, and `identity-correspondence.mjs` signs and verifies over the stored secret half.

Structurally identical, fail-closed both ways. The structural transition rules run *before* both
checks and keep Deep's own refusal names, so a caller can tell a rule violation from an unavailable
primitive. **No hybrid control rotation is claimed as verified by this lane**: the court's honest
rotation arm passes injected test doubles for both, prints
`CAPABILITIES: … ml-dsa-65=INJECTED-TEST-DOUBLE ed25519-point=INJECTED-TEST-DOUBLE`, and three
separate arms assert the fail-closed refusals. The Ed25519 half of that arm *is* real — the court
flips one signature byte and `node:crypto` catches it.

The parts of the hybrid suite this closure **can** compute exactly, it does: `rootKeySetId` and
`identityControlDigest` are pure SHA-256 over canonical JSON with no curve arithmetic, and both match
Deep's values at the pin.

### 3.3 The store is read-only

Deep's `local-control-store.mjs` creates, publishes and rotates a controller. This lane only reads.
Provisioning a controller is a custody act, so the only writer remains Deep's own. Disposable
identities for the court are built by `scripts/aumlok/make-disposable-identity.mjs`, which is
labelled test-only, has no default destination, refuses an existing directory, and registers a **real
corresponding ML-DSA-65 keypair** — generated from a test seed and proven to correspond before the
record is opened, using the same `lib/pq-generator.mjs` the binding ceremony uses. The court's
fully-real hybrid identity produced by Deep at the pin remains a separate arm.

`loadLocalAumlokPublicControl` requires the private fields to be *present* (the field set is closed)
but never decodes or returns them. A separate, named reader (`readLocalAumlokFullRecord`) returns them to
the correspondence check in `identity-correspondence.mjs`, which decodes and verifies them. Deep does check it; the removal is stated here and in
the `SAME_UID_POSIX_MODE_ONLY` ceiling rather than quietly dropped.

**Measured consequence, added after the ML-DSA-65 binding repair, and it is not a small one.**
Repointing only `mlDsa65SecretKeyHex` — keeping the canonical encoding and the exact byte length —
leaves `scripts/aumlok/project.mjs` returning **exit 0** with a full projection, while Deep's own
`loadLocalAumlokControl` on the same directory refuses
`aumlok-local:entry-malformed` (`malformed key s1/s3 … outside of ETA range`). So binding now
refuses to *write* a non-corresponding pair, but this lane's reader does not *detect* one. That is a
deliberate consequence of the reader never decoding private material, and it is a **divergence from
Deep**, not a gap this change closes. A record can also be written by another writer — Deep's own
store, an earlier version of `bind`, or an editor — and the reader will project it. Closing this
means either decoding the secret half in a read path or refusing to project when the halves are
unproven. `project.mjs` still projects a record whose secret halves do not correspond;
`scripts/aumlok/verify-identity --read-secret-half` checks correspondence over the stored bytes and
refuses by name (court: `tests/aukora-aumlok-approve.test.mjs`).

### 3.4 The projection is seven fields, not five

Deep's `projectDeveloperAumlok` yields `{subject, epoch, activeControlDigest, grantDomain,
custodyClass}`. This lane yields `{domain, subject, epoch, activeControlDigest, revoked,
approvalKeyDid, custodyClass}`:

* **`revoked` is added.** Deep's `readControl` throws on a revoked head, so a revoked subject is
  unrepresentable there; the host and KIRA both need to render "revoked" without an exception.
  `admitPublicControl` refuses a revoked projection by name, so exposing the fact does not admit it.
* **`approvalKeyDid` is added** — D1's requirement, and the layer join in §2.
* **`grantDomain` is deliberately not carried.** It names the grant-v5 authority domain, and identity
  must never carry an authority field: *"identity is an edge that receipts may name. It never
  authorizes."* The mapping to Deep's five-field row is therefore: drop `grantDomain`, add
  `revoked` and `approvalKeyDid`. It is recorded here as a measurement and is not implemented as a
  function, so no caller can obtain an authority-shaped record from this adapter by accident.
* **`domain` is added** so a serialized projection is self-describing and cannot be confused with a
  control head.

## 5. The D2 approval channel, and what it is measured against

D2's signer is this lane's own design; Deep has no equivalent module at the pin. What it *is*
measured against is the same registered key and the same public projection, plus Genesis's own
Ed25519 action-signer layer:

| D2 requirement | Where it lives | Measured by |
|---|---|---|
| exact signed bytes, including operation digest, challenge and expiry | `lib/owner-approval.mjs` → `approvalSigningBytes` = `'aukora:owner-approval-signature:v1' + NUL + canonicalJSON(request)` | five arms, one per substituted axis; plus an arm that re-derives the preimage independently of the session and verifies the returned signature over it |
| challenge | 32-byte CSPRNG nonce, generated per approval, consumed exactly once | replay arm (the same pair accepted twice → `aumlok:approval-replayed`), challenge-mismatch arm, and an arm that a challenge consumed by a *failed* verification is not reusable |
| expiry | checked by the signer before signing and by the broker after the round trip | `signer:request-expired` and `aumlok:approval-expired`, both by name |
| registered-key verification | Ed25519 under the key decoded from `projection.approvalKeyDid` (`lib/signer-channel.mjs`) | a real flipped-byte signature is refused; a signer holding a *different* registered key produces a signature the broker refuses |
| explicit channel failures | `APPROVAL_REFUSE` — ten stable names, plus the two not-ready names (`aumlok:unbound`, `aumlok:no-seed`) passed through as themselves | absent socket, silent listener, garbage listener and a declining signer are four distinct arms, none of which throws |
| test keys only | `scripts/aumlok/signer.mjs` has no default key path, requires `--key-file`, and checks owner/mode/symlink | five daemon-guard arms, including a non-`0600` key file and a key that is not the registered one |

**The one seam with Genesis's existing action signer.** Not changed, not duplicated: the D2 signer
signs an *approval*, and Genesis's composition gate signs *grants*
(`scripts/composition/ed25519.py`, `grant.py`). They share only the primitive — Ed25519, which here
is `node:crypto`/OpenSSL rather than the gate's stdlib implementation, because this lane runs in the
host's Node process. Two implementations of the same RFC is a deliberate non-duplication: the gate
must be dependency-free Python, and this lane must be dependency-free Node. Neither replaces the
other, and no grant is produced or consumed here.

**What the status lines say, and why they are not bare tokens.** D2 asks for `OWNER_KEY_SIGNED`,
`OWNER_KEY_SAME_UID`, `SIGNER_DEVICE_TRUSTED`, `ATTENDANCE_REPORTED_NOT_PROVEN` and
`SUCCESSION_UNMEASURED`. Printing `SIGNER_DEVICE_TRUSTED` as though the device were trusted would be
a claim nothing measured, so each token is printed with its honest value:
`OWNER_KEY_SIGNED` as the condition under which it is earned, `OWNER_KEY_SAME_UID: true`,
`SIGNER_DEVICE_TRUSTED: not-established (D3)`, and the other two as `true` statements about what is
*not* claimed. Two arms assert the device line is never printed as established.

**The approver, and what is deliberately absent.** `createOwnerSigner` requires a `review` procedure
and has no default, so `signer:no-reviewer` is a real refusal and an unconfigured signer cannot
approve by omission. `scripts/aumlok/signer.mjs` has three approver modes: `test-all` (labelled
`NOT a human review`), `decline-all`, and `popup`, which raises a native `osascript` dialog showing the
canonical request and challenge before signing. No court drives the popup branch or asserts its text
**[CODE ONLY]**. The popup is presentation, not a security boundary: it runs in the same process and UID
as the key. A real decision procedure is supplied in code. Nothing here
implements, implies or fakes D2's "presents the operation" or D3's hardware custody.

## 6. Reproducing the compatibility claim

```bash
# 1. The lane's courts, standalone: no Deep, no network, no sibling checkout.
node tests/aukora-aumlok.test.mjs            # 137 arms (run 2026-09-26 at 674fae6bf)
node tests/aukora-aumlok.test.mjs --mutate   # 143 arms: five mutation arms plus 'no mutation was missed'
node tests/aukora-aumlok-signer.test.mjs     # 93 arms (99 with --mutate), real Unix sockets and real Ed25519

# 1b. The mount, which needs a HOST and therefore a release. It materializes one from this
#     checkout if none is named, and REFUSES rather than skipping if neither is possible.
AUKORA_DSH_RELEASE=<release> node tests/aukora-aumlok-mount.test.mjs   # 22 arms

# 1c. The diagnostic: which of the three things is actually true. Read-only.
node scripts/aumlok/diagnose.mjs --release <release>   # packaged adapter / mounted signer / custody

# 2. The fixture against Deep itself (reviewer step; needs a Deep checkout at the pin).
node scripts/aumlok/regenerate-deep-vectors.mjs --deep <deep-checkout> --check

# 3. The lane's front door, on disposable state.
D=$(mktemp -d)/identity
node scripts/aumlok/make-disposable-identity.mjs --directory "$D"
node scripts/aumlok/project.mjs "$D"
```

Expected from step 1: `AUMLOK ADAPTER: GREEN` with `MUTATION ARMS: 5 run, 5 detected, 0 missed`, and
`AUMLOK SIGNER: GREEN`, all exit 0. A missing mutation target (stale mutation text) is reported as a
failure, never skipped.
